data.reasoning: The PKGBUILD is a standard Python package build from PyPI (files.pythonhosted.org) with a pinned SHA256 checksum. The deepseek-v4-flash model successfully reviewed all 4 maintainer files (.SRCINFO, .nvchecker.toml, .gitignore, PKGBUILD) and found no security issues. The qwen3-235b model's inconclusive result was due to API errors (HTTP 400) on .gitignore and .nvchecker.toml, not actual security concerns - it successfully reviewed the PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO as safe. The openrouter/free report is advisory-only (advisory: true) and for a different version (0.8.2 vs 0.12.0), so it doesn't count toward the verdict. No malicious code execution, no suspicious network activity, no injection patterns detected.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by tool failures, not security findings. qwen3-235b encountered HTTP 400 errors when auditing .gitignore and .nvchecker.toml, resulting in an inconclusive verdict despite successfully reviewing the PKGBUILD as safe. deepseek-v4-flash completed all file reviews successfully and returned safe. The openrouter/free report is advisory-only and for a different package version.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b: API errors (HTTP 400) prevented review of .gitignore and .nvchecker.toml
openrouter/free: Only reviewed PKGBUILD, skipped upstream tarball (correct behavior), but had parsing error on PKGBUILD review
learnings: API errors should be distinguished from security findings - tool failures causing inconclusive results should not block a safe verdict when other models successfully complete the audit
Advisory reports for different package versions should be clearly separated from the current audit to avoid confusion
Standard PyPI packages with pinned checksums are low-risk and models should recognize this pattern quickly without over-analysis
